### Real Estate Workflow and Computer Usage

Realtors operate in a high-pressure, mobile-first environment where administrative "digital sprawl" often competes with revenue-generating activities like prospecting and client meetings.

#### Most Time-Consuming Computer Tasks
The primary friction for realtors is the manual, repetitive nature of administrative work, often referred to as "Tier 2" or "Tier 3" tasks.
*   **Documentation & Data Entry:** Manually syncing property data across platforms (MLS, Zillow, Realtor.com, brokerage sites) and updating CRMs are significant time sinks.
*   **Email Management:** Constant, reactive email checking is a major productivity killer. High-producing agents mitigate this by "batching" emails into specific time windows (e.g., early afternoon) rather than responding as messages arrive.
*   **Transaction Coordination:** Managing contracts, signatures, and deadlines requires constant document preparation and follow-up.
*   **Lead Management:** Triaging inbound leads from multiple web forms and portals manually takes hours each week.

#### App Stack on Mac
Because most modern real estate software is browser-based, agents rely heavily on web-optimized workflows on their Macs.
*   **CRM & Lead Management:** *Follow Up Boss* is widely cited as an agent favorite. Other common platforms include *BoldTrail* (formerly kvCORE) and *CINC* for integrated IDX websites and lead funnels.
*   **Transaction & Signing:** *Dotloop* is used for end-to-end transaction management (keeping documents in a "loop"), while *DocuSign* remains the industry standard for standalone e-signatures.
*   **Marketing:** *Canva* is the primary tool for creating listing flyers, social media graphics, and short videos.
*   **Daily Organization:** *Google Workspace* (Calendar, Gmail, Drive) is essential for scheduling and document storage. *SupaSidebar* is a niche tool used by some Mac users to organize browser tabs across different clients or listings.
*   **Note:** Native Mac apps are less common than browser-based tools, as agents prioritize cross-device accessibility.

#### Key Statistics
| Metric | Source |
| :--- | :--- |
| **19.5 hours** per week are lost on average by agents to administrative tasks (CRM logging, calls, scheduling). | Pitchit.ai (2026) |
| **65% of the workweek** is spent on administrative tasks, leaving only 35% for actual selling. | ArmaSourcing (2026) |
| **28% of the workweek** is spent managing email by average workers. | McKinsey Global Institute |
| **30 out of 40 hours** required for an average real estate transaction are purely administrative/unlicensed tasks. | Avenue Transactions (2024) |

#### Caveats
*   **Definitions of "Admin":** Sources vary on what constitutes "administrative" work. Some include phone-based lead follow-up, while others classify that as part of the sales process.
*   **Technology Adoption:** There is a significant divide between top-producing agents who use automated systems/AI and average agents who rely on manual, legacy workflows, which accounts for the wide range in reported time spent on admin.
